THEORY

The titration between bench alkali and bench acid or bench alkali and dilute acid does not give correct titre value. This is because a small volume of the bench acid or bench alkali is consumed by a large volume of the dilute acid. A very small volumetric error, therefore, gives a different resulting strength. Hence, correct titre value is obtained when the dilute solutions are titrated. For this reason, double titration is performed. At first, bench alkali is titrated against dilute acid to have only one rough reading. Then the approximate strength of the bench alkali is determined.
